title: Balanced, Yet Moving
question: Does being in balance mean standing still?
hook: A child zooming down a slide is perfectly balanced.
idea: A system is in mechanical equilibrium when the net force on every part is zero, which allows steady motion as well as rest, and a small nudge decides whether it is stable.

beats.prompt: A marble sits at the very top of a smooth upside-down bowl and gets a tiny nudge. What happens?

choices.label: It rolls back to the top
choices.feedback: Restoring forces belong to a low point, not a hilltop.

choices.label: It stays wherever it was nudged
choices.feedback: That describes a flat, neutral spot; the top of a bowl is not flat.

beats.explain: At a local maximum of potential energy, a small displacement makes forces push the system even farther away, an unstable equilibrium.

beats.prompt: Sort each case: is it in mechanical equilibrium?
items: Stone speeding up as it falls
beats.explain: Equilibrium needs zero net force, so constant velocity counts, while collapsing or speeding up does not.

beats.prompt: Match each situation to its type of equilibrium.
pairs: Potential energy at a local minimum
Potential energy at a local maximum
beats.explain: The shape of the potential energy around a point tells you how it responds to a small nudge.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: A particle is in mechanical equilibrium when the net force on it is zero.
So a book resting on a table is in equilibrium.
A child sliding at constant speed also has a constant velocity.
So the child cannot be in equilibrium, because she is moving.
beats.explain: Constant velocity means zero net force, so a moving child is in mechanical equilibrium but not in static equilibrium.
